title: Pipeline Architecture: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Where The T Happens | the same pipeline drawn as ETL and as ELT, and what is still on disk three weeks later | ELT's advantage is not speed, it is that the raw data survives your next parsing bug

2. Three Zones Ladder | one record climbing staging -> raw -> curated, with lifetime and readers per zone | staging is deletable scaffolding, raw is the archive you must protect, curated is the only surface you promise stability on

3. The Backfill Rescue | the July click_position bug, with and without a raw zone, as the discovery date slides | with raw, recovery cost is flat at one backfill query; without it, the loss grows every day you fail to notice

4. Contract Gate | five proposed producer changes run through the v3 contract check | backward compatible means every existing consumer keeps working — additive-optional passes, rename/retype/enum-widening does not
